description:
The install wall was "first set up Quicklisp".  Vendor cl-ppcre in the tree and
have cl/pcl-runtime.lisp put that directory on ASDF's central registry before
its asdf:load-system, keeping ASDF's ordinary search (distro package,
Quicklisp, ~/.sbclrc) as the fallback.

=== DONE (s481a) ===

WHICH COPY, and it mattered.  The box loads Debian's `cl-ppcre` package, whose
.asd reports version 2.1.2 -- but it is NOT the v2.1.2 tag: it is upstream
master at commit a2ea581c23fdc184168423adbd4b4c1f48d42743 (2025-06-06), and the
tag differs in optimize.lisp and closures.lisp.  All 17 .lisp files plus
cl-ppcre.asd are byte-identical (cmp) to that commit's tarball, so the library
under PCL did not change; vendoring the tag would have been a silent library
change riding a packaging commit.  Only the cl-ppcre system is carried (not
cl-ppcre-unicode, the tests or the docs -- asdf:already-loaded-systems is
"asdf uiop asdf-package-system cl-ppcre"), plus LICENSE and CHANGELOG.
cl/vendor/README.md is the stamp and says the directory is never edited here.

THE DIRECTORY IS DERIVED FROM THE RUNTIME'S OWN LOAD LOCATION
(*load-truename* / *compile-file-truename*), never $PCL_ROOT: a checkout, a
worktree and an installation each load their own runtime and must get the
library beside it.  Verified on a real install --
ISRC=<prefix>/lib/pcl/cl/vendor/cl-ppcre/.  install-pcl needed no change (its
@TREE copies cl/ recursively).

THE SAVED CORE KEYS ON IT.  Vendored sources are compiled INTO the core, so
PCLSbcl::_vendor_stamp folds the cl/vendor/ tree's CONTENT (not mtimes) into
the core's name; CORE_KEY_VERSION 1 -> 2.

#1461's BMH shadow still holds against the vendored version (BMH-ON=t BUILT=1
SHADOW=t); its docstring's "not a vendored copy" is corrected, and the pin
stays because the FALLBACK can still be any version.

Also: ASDF's :silent covers ASDF's chatter, not SBCL's compiler notes, and the
one-per-machine compile of the vendored sources is now ours -- its optimization
notes are muffled (warnings and errors are not).

tools/lib/PCLLicense.pm gained %EXCLUDE_TREES: cl/vendor/ sits INSIDE a scanned
root (cl/), so it needs a prune where perl-tests/ and cpan-tests/ merely are not
in @ROOTS.  A pruned tree must still exist -- new row in Pl/t/license-tag-01.t.

GUARD Pl/t/vendored-ppcre-01.t (8 rows, ~11 s): every leg runs with $HOME
pointed at a fresh EMPTY directory and CL_SOURCE_REGISTRY set to ignore
inherited configuration, so no ~/.sbclrc, no Quicklisp and no distro package can
answer -- source mode, the cached-core path, which source directory ASDF loaded,
and the BMH pin.  Inverse-verified on a bb5a6d77 archive: 8/8 FAIL there, at
"PCL: ASDF could not load cl-ppcre", which is the install wall itself.

MEASURED: core build 3.9 s, install 5.1 s, bench json-rt 1.72x / textproc 3.27x
(Fable's quiet-box board the same session: 1.85x / 3.40x) -- within noise.
docs/caching.md gained SS1a "Where cl-ppcre comes from"; docs/pcl-commands.md
names it in the runtime section and in FILES.
subject: P1(a): vendor cl-ppcre under cl/vendor/cl-ppcre/ so a machine needs SBCL and nothing else -- the runtime pushes it onto asdf:*central-registry*, ASDF's own search stays as the fallback
